initial_scene: A seated humanoid faces the camera across a tabletop. A red multimeter rests at robot-right on the small black tabletop patch, with its black hinged stand visibly extended. The dark right hand is on image left; the white left hand is on image right.

observed_sequence.action: The right arm extends toward the meter at robot-right; left hand remains near the lap. The meter is already raised on its extended black rear stand.
The right fingers close around the red housing, with the thumb opposing them on the body. The table and stand still support the device during grasp establishment. Left hand does not contact it.

The right hand lifts the meter clear, briefly lowers/repositions it above the tabletop, and starts rolling the whole body. The stand is visibly free-hanging from its hinge. Left hand remains near the lap and is not supporting the meter.

The right hand raises and rolls the device into a near-horizontal rear-facing pose. The rear housing rectangle, black back panel and yellow hinge landmark turn with the housing; these whole-object changes should not be mistaken for left-hand mechanism actuation. Left arm rises with fingers open and still separated from the meter.

The right hand moves the meter up toward the chest and rolls it from near horizontal to diagonal, presenting its back with the stand projecting toward the approaching left hand. The right hand retains the body grasp.
Left fingers approach and make brief contact around the free end of the extended black stand. Right fingers continue holding the red body. Exact fingertip opposition is partly hidden.

The left fingers open and shift upward and outward from the stand tip, with a visible separation during part of this interval; they then return toward the same free end. Right hand alone retains and bears the body, making small pose adjustments.

The left fingers curl around the free end of the black stand, retaining contact while the right hand holds the housing diagonally. This is a mechanism contact, not a transfer of the device body or visible front-dial manipulation.

The left hand changes finger/wrist orientation and moves the stand end downward toward the back of the meter, while the right hand keeps its housing grasp and tilts the whole meter slightly. Relative to the red housing and yellow hinge landmark, the black plate changes from projecting transversely outward to lying closer along the long axis/back of the housing: an inward pivot distinct from whole-object rolling. The final hinge seating is partly hidden.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for direction; medium for detailed contact

observed_sequence.action: The left hand releases the stand and separates; the right hand rolls the meter away from the left hand while retaining the same body grasp. The left never receives the meter.
The right arm transports the meter down to the original table area and turns its long body toward a more horizontal placement pose. The left hand lowers without supporting the meter.
The right hand lowers the body close to the tabletop, opens and withdraws. The released device tips/rolls from its edge and settles with the front display/control face upward.
The meter remains released face-up on the tabletop; the right arm retreats and both hands return near the lap. No further object manipulation occurs.

It releases before the right returns the meter to the table. It does not visibly grasp or manipulate the front dial.
